request.spec:
Every change that alters any person's claimed or due-total is followed in the audit, after the
change's own lines, by one line per person whose figures changed: ROLLUP name=<name>
claimed=<claimed> due-total=<due-total>, people in the order they were added, a person who did
not exist before the change counting as changed; then, when the sheet's claimed-total or
due-total changed, one line TOTALS claimed-total=<total> due-total=<total>. A change that moves
no figure adds no such line (setting a rate to the value it already has, settling a claim whose
frozen figure equals its live one, re-stating a person whose figures did not move). Changing the
sheet's today is a change like any other and is followed by these lines when figures move, with
no line of its own.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The rollup audit lines are in, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec on the first run.

**How it works**
- **New `rollup` package** (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/`): a `Rollup` service works out each person's claimed and due-total, and the sheet's two totals, the same way the screen does. That covers n/a (no rate for the grade today and no settled or stated figure to keep), the settled or stated figure taking precedence, the rate in force on the claim's date, and rounding half to even.
- **Two new steps in each change's pipeline.** `SnapshotRollup` records the figures just before the change writes anything. `RecordRollup` runs after the change's own audit line. It writes one `ROLLUP … person=<name> claimed=… due-total=…` line per person whose figures moved, in the order people were added; a newly added person always counts as moved. Then it writes `TOTALS … claimed-total=… due-total=…` if either total moved.
  - The steps are in eight endpoints: add or edit a person, add or edit a claim, change a claim's status, take a statement, set a rate, and change today.
  - A refused change throws before `RecordRollup`, so it writes no rollup lines.
  - A change that moves no figure writes none either.
- **Changing today.** The request didn't say who made it, so the screen now sends the signed-in user as `by`. Its validator now refuses a request without a user, like the other changes do. It still writes no line of its own, only the rollup lines when figures move.

One thing to keep in mind: the figure logic now exists twice, once on the server for the audit and once in the front end for the screen (`features/rates/rates.slot.tsx`). If the due rules change, both need updating.
